evidence.result_summary: claims has source_billing_rowid, billing_amount, insurance_provider, medical_condition, etc. denials has claim_id (FK to claims), denial_reason_code, denial_amount.

evidence.step: 1b. Confirm schema of upstream tables before querying them
evidence.result_summary: mart_billing: billing_amount REAL (no explicit FK column, sqlite implicit rowid). staging_patients: billing_amount TEXT, no FK column. raw_patients: billing_amount TEXT, no FK column, no schema pointer to further upstream.
4 upstream datasets: mart_billing (degree 1), mart_demographics (degree 1), staging_patients (degree 2), raw_patients (degree 3).

evidence.result_summary: Single dataset-level path: raw_patients -> staging_patients -> mart_billing -> claims.

evidence.result_summary: 0 upstream entities returned -- raw_patients is the root of the registered pipeline.

evidence.query_or_call: SELECT DISTINCT insurance_provider/medical_condition FROM claims WHERE ... LIKE '%igna%'/'%besi%'

evidence.step: 3b. Break down flagged segment's denials by reason code
evidence.query_or_call: SELECT d.denial_reason_code, COUNT(*) FROM claims c JOIN denials d ON d.claim_id=c.claim_id WHERE insurance_provider='Cigna' AND medical_condition='obesity' GROUP BY d.denial_reason_code
evidence.result_summary: INVALID_BILLING_AMOUNT=280, HIGH_RISK_SCORE=11, RANDOM_AUDIT=7 (sums to Sentinel's 298 denied).

evidence.step: 3c. Confirm INVALID_BILLING_AMOUNT claims actually have billing_amount<0 in claims
evidence.query_or_call: SELECT COUNT(*), SUM(CASE WHEN billing_amount<0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) FROM claims JOIN denials ... WHERE denial_reason_code='INVALID_BILLING_AMOUNT'

evidence.step: 4a. Test reproduction at immediate upstream hop (mart_billing)
evidence.query_or_call: LEFT JOIN mart_billing mb ON mb.rowid = c.source_billing_rowid; count mb.billing_amount<0 and missing joins
evidence.result_summary: 280/280 negative in mart_billing, 0 missing joins -- reproduces 100% at first hop.

evidence.step: 4b. Verify mart_billing.rowid aligns with staging_patients.rowid before trusting next hop
evidence.query_or_call: JOIN staging_patients sp ON sp.rowid=mb.rowid; compare date_of_admission, discharge_date, numeric billing_amount
evidence.result_summary: 55500/55500 rows align on dates and numeric billing_amount -- rowid join to staging_patients is valid (an earlier text-equality check on billing_amount undercounted due to TEXT vs REAL formatting, not misalignment).

evidence.query_or_call: LEFT JOIN staging_patients sp ON sp.rowid = c.source_billing_rowid; count CAST(sp.billing_amount AS REAL)<0
evidence.result_summary: 280/280 negative in staging_patients, 0 missing joins -- still reproduces 100%.

evidence.step: 4d. Verify staging_patients.rowid aligns with raw_patients.rowid before trusting next hop
evidence.query_or_call: JOIN raw_patients rp ON rp.rowid=sp.rowid; compare dates and numeric billing_amount
evidence.result_summary: 55500/55500 rows align -- rowid join to raw_patients is valid.

evidence.step: 4e. Test reproduction at raw_patients (final available hop)
evidence.query_or_call: LEFT JOIN raw_patients rp ON rp.rowid = c.source_billing_rowid; count CAST(rp.billing_amount AS REAL)<0
evidence.result_summary: 280/280 negative in raw_patients, 0 missing joins -- reproduces 100% all the way to the pipeline root.

investigator.root_cause_summary: Sentinel flagged Cigna/obesity for a 15.99% denial rate (4.2x baseline). Breaking the 298 denials down by reason code shows 280 (93.96%) are INVALID_BILLING_AMOUNT, with a smaller unrelated remainder of 11 HIGH_RISK_SCORE and 7 RANDOM_AUDIT denials that have no field-level defect to trace by design. For the 280 INVALID_BILLING_AMOUNT claims, billing_amount < 0 was checked at every hop of the confirmed lineage chain (claims -> mart_billing -> staging_patients -> raw_patients), verifying row alignment via rowid at each hop before trusting the count. The negative value reproduces at exactly 280/280 (100%) at every single hop, including raw_patients, which has no further upstream lineage registered. This means the bad data was never introduced by any transform in this pipeline -- it is already present in the earliest available source data. The elevated denial rate for this segment is a downstream symptom of a pre-existing data-quality defect inherited from raw_patients, not a bug introduced by mart_billing, staging_patients, or the claims derivation itself.
